pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/83534. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/89226 is a related change wrt. perf.

This PR aims to solve the incremental generation perf issue in the config binding generator, so that diffs in input compilations that don't change prior effective inputs the generator (or the resulting output) do not cause regeneration.

It also moves Roslyn helpers, generator helpers, and the `TypeRef` identity token to common locations to be shared by the JSON and config binding generators.

issue_context.title: Iterate on config binding generator parsing pipeline to benefit from input caching provided by the incremental-generator feature
issue_context.body: Address feedback from @eiriktsarpalis and @sharwell in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/82179#pullrequestreview-1339250948 and related discussions.

Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-extensions-configuration See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
Address feedback from @eiriktsarpalis in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/82179#pullrequestreview-1339250948 and related discussions.
Author: layomia
Assignees: layomia
Labels: `area-Extensions-Configuration`, `source-generator`
Milestone: 8.0.0

Triage: moving this issue to 9.0, mitigating 8.0 parsing perf with https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/90619.
- We haven't had customer reports of the performance problems driving this issue.  This effort is preemptive based on best practice / code-review.  
- Generator is off-by default. If enabled and perf issues arise, a workaround would be as follows:
  - for projects with no binding, disable the generator
  - for project with binding, remove it from design time builds with an MSBuild target

From @jaredpar in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/90835/files#r1303627652. Address in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/89587:

> The equals implementation on BinderInvocation uses ref equality, not value equality. That means the CreateSyntaxProvider call above is never cached. This is an issue for IDE performance.

review_comments: Why mark the helpers internal when the type itself is public?
The helpers are currently only used internally.
`BinderInvocation` is not equatable, so the following steps will never be able to be cut off.

Yes this can be refactored so that we can return an incremental value at each pipeline stage. Seems like this would only be for "purity": 

> so the following steps will never be able to be cut off.

I'm not sure how we can have meaningful intermediate phases with this incremental pipeline.. we still need to parse the entire object graph for each target config type per invocation.
This will change any time the file is edited.
This is particularly concerning because it means that typing in _any_ file with an error will cause the entire pipeline to never be equal.
Resolved elsewhere.

IOperations are not safe to store in models, just like symbols or any other direct semantic info. `IOperation`s are particularly bad, as they only consider referential equality, and they are specific to a semantic model.

note: diagnostics in incremental SGs are hard (especially as basically any edit invalidates them).  consider moving diagnostics, if possible, to just an analyzer that runs independently.  The analyzer can, of course, share code with the SG, esp. in the form of helper functions.

If the diagnostics are part of the equatable incremental model, shouldn't that suffice to keep them up-to-date? IOW if an edit did trigger invalidation, then the set of diagnostics would differ from that of the cached incremental value, triggering an update to the new set downstream.

There's obviously [this issue](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/68291) to be mindful of, which is why we're using the `DiagnosticInfo` record here instead.

> IOW if an edit did trigger invalidation, then the set of diagnostics would differ from that of the cached incremental value, triggering an update to the new set downstream.

This is my experience as well, so I'll leave as-is in this PR.

~~Having a separate analyzer in the future seems like a nice idea if we can develop a clean, shared parsing abstraction with the generator implementation.~~ Consensus is that a separate diagnostic analyzer is the way to go.

An edit will _always_ trigger an invalidation if there are any diagnostics. `Location` (which is part of both `DiagnosticInfo` and `Diagnostic`) will never compare equal when a file edit happens, so if there any diagnosics in the pipeline it will always break.
Resolved in a few threads.
`CompilationData` is not equatable, so this is going to retrigger on every keystroke.
Is this checking for rank > 1?
Yes, in the `CreateArraySpec` method.
Testing removal of `EraseCompileTimeMetadata` - https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/89587#discussion_r1334692857.
Likewise, I believe the regex generator defines such a struct as well.

At a glance this seems like a type that would be defined as a `record` if arrays were naturally equitable. Why wasn't this just defined as a `record` with `ImmutableEquatableArray<object?>` wrapping `MessageArgs`?

It would force an intermediate allocation from `object[]` to `ImmutableEquatableArray` then back to an `object[]` when the `Diagnostic` gets materialized. I think it's small enough to justify a bespoke type. Longer term though we should be looking at addressing https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/68291 and use `Diagnostic` in the equatable models directly.

`Diagnostic` will never be ok to use in a model. `Location` has a reference to the `SyntaxTree` that it was created from, and that will change every time the file changes. This wrapper has similar issues: even if message args compared correctly, it would still be broken for equality.

> Diagnostic will never be ok to use in a model. 

Per https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/89587#discussion_r1334856473 this bit is mitigated for this PR, follow up in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/92509.

Can we add a test that verifies that the false edits (replace source code with exact same source code) cause the source generator to do no work? Essentially verifying that incremental edits are handled correctly in the generator?
It would be good to not need to `Collect` here. Because we call `Collect`, it eliminates any possibility of incrementality if _any_ intercepted call changes.

It would seem like the initial `IncrementalValuesProvider` node would contain as many elements as there are invocation expressions in the current compilation, with substantial filtering happening in this `Where` clause?

I wonder if there are any performance implications with incremental values holding so many values. Is there any way we could make the predicate more precise (e.g. by peeking at the method name being invoked?)

cc @chsienki @CyrusNajmabadi

I haven't looked at the pr at all, but the following is likely very bad: 

> would contain as many elements as there are invocation expressions in the current compilation, 

This will be enormous, and will likely be recomputed on every edit.  Almost certainly not ok. 

I can look more deeply at the actual pr tomorrow.

~~The list is [pre-filtered](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d5b41307d26cfe28b05354ea4bb1eba2a7eea27f/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder/gen/Helpers/Parser/CandidateBinderInvocation.cs#L18-L20.) using name matches and should only contain invocations that are very like the binding calls we  care about. I should be able to remove the `Where` clause.~~

Even if the `CandidateBinderInvocation.Create` correctly detects that and returns null, it still results in a very large set of incremental values that is mostly nulls. Making the filtering predicate in line 36 more precise would go a long way in reducing the number of elements in that initial incremental value.
Nit: unless these are being reused, why not just inline in the tests for easier reading?
In general, they are being reused. I'll inline any single-use ones.
